newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss recognise Yugoslavia, seek refugees' return.
newsitem.headline: Swiss recognise Yugoslavia, seek refugees' return.

text.p: Switzerland has decided to recognise rump Yugoslavia and will resume diplomatic relations with Belgrade, the foreign ministry in Berne said on Wednesday.

The move follows similar action by several European countries after European Union foreign ministers agreed in December to restore diplomatic ties with rump Yugoslavia, which now consists of Serbia and Montenegro.
These countries have acknowledged rump Yugoslavia as the successor state to former Yugoslavia, whose disintegration in 1991 touched off ethnic war among Serbs, Croats and Moslems.

"In its official announcement to authorities in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the Federal Council (cabinet) will express its expectation that the FRY recognise and implement its obligation under international law to take back all its citizens staying in Switzerland without a residence permit," it added.
Switzerland hosts nearly 19,000 Yugoslav citizens who have had their requests for asylum rejected and must now leave the country, federal officials said.
